s2: add Encode/Decode for ShapeIndex

ShapeIndex can now be serialized to an io.Writer and restored from an
io.Reader without rebuilding. The encoding stores every shape keyed by
its shape ID (all built-in Shape types, plus a generic fallback for any
other in-package Shape) and the complete cell structure, so a decoded
index is immediately fresh and usable for queries and iteration.

Encode applies pending updates first, so an index that was never
explicitly built still encodes completely. Decode validates all counts,
IDs, cell ordering, and edge references, grows slices incrementally to
avoid untrusted large allocations, and returns errors on malformed input.

Also make applyUpdatesInternal iterate up to nextID rather than
len(shapes), so shapes added after a removed ID are not skipped, and
reset the pending update state in Reset.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
`ShapeIndex` now has `Encode(io.Writer)` and `Decode(io.Reader)`, committed as `6dfab1b` on a new branch `shapeindex-encoding`. The repo has no `main` branch, locally or on any remote, so I branched from `master`. The full test suite passes.

**What it does** (code is in `s2/shapeindex_encode.go`):
- **Shapes and IDs:** every shape is saved under its original ID, so cells still point at the right shapes after decoding. All built-in types come back as the same type: `Polygon`, `Loop`, `Polyline`, `PointVector`, `LaxPolyline`, `LaxLoop` and `LaxPolygon`. Any other shape type in the package, such as the test-only `edgeVectorShape`, is saved by its edges and chains and comes back as a generic shape that behaves the same.
- **Cell structure:** the full cell structure is saved, so a decoded index can be queried and iterated straight away, without `Build`.
- **No explicit `Build`:** `Encode` applies any pending updates first, so an index that was never built still encodes completely.
- **Edge cases:** an empty index still produces bytes. Shapes with no edges and shapes with different chain counts round-trip.
- **Bad input:** `Decode` returns errors instead of panicking. It checks all counts, IDs, cell order and overlap, and edge references. It caps how much it allocates up front and only grows as real data arrives, so a fake huge count can't force a huge allocation.
- **Format:** it's a versioned, Go-only format and isn't compatible with the C++ library's encoded shape index.

**Tests:** in `s2/shapeindex_encode_test.go`, covering every shape type, encoding without `Build`, gaps in shape IDs, empty shapes, truncation at every byte, single-byte corruption at every position, and oversized counts. I also ran a throwaway fuzz pass of 200k random corruptions with no panics; that test isn't committed.

**Two small fixes in `shapeindex.go`:**
- Building now loops up to the next shape ID instead of the number of shapes. Before, removing a shape before the first build meant later shapes were never indexed.
- `Reset` now clears pending-update state, so shapes added after a reset get indexed.

**Problems already in the library, not fixed:**
- **Removing a shape after `Build` doesn't update the cells**; that part of the code was never written. So cells can still list the removed shape. `Encode` leaves those stale entries out, so a decoded index only refers to shapes it actually has.
- **Adding shapes to an index that's already built hangs**, because it tries to take a lock it already holds. Fixing the lock only exposed a panic in more unfinished code, so I reverted that change. In practice this means you can query and iterate a decoded index, but adding shapes to it will hit the same hang.
